column2: Software Development using AI
UG

This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with coding agents. It covers how to configure agent skills and tool use protocols, translate requirements into executable specifications, analyze execution traces from automated agent workflows, and assess pipelines integrating automated testing and reliability checks. Students will be able to configure agent skills and tool use protocols using an orchestration framework, translate natural language requirements into executable specifications, analyze execution traces to identify failure causes, and assess AI-native development pipelines. The course is taught through lectures, tutorials, and laboratory sessions emphasizing hands-on project work and developer workflows.

Course Code: Configure agent skills, tool use protocols, and context engineering mechanisms for coding agents, using an agent orchestration framework, such that the configured agents successfully execute supplied coding tasks meeting functional specifications.
column2: Translate natural language software requirements into executable specifications and structured development plans, using spec-driven development tools, covering every use case in the supplied requirements document.
column3: Analyze execution traces and feedback loops from automated agent workflows, using log analysis tools for a supplied software factory artifact of at most 1000 lines of code, identifying at least three distinct failure causes with supporting log evidence.
column4: Assess an AI-native software development pipeline integrating automated testing, evaluation, and reliability checks, justifying each assessment decision against at least one stated reliability requirement.
